High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore

sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 5 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 2088 of 2022
 Smt. Saraswatinbai
 Versus
 Arvind And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Sameer Verma, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the respond
 Order

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 10.3.2022 passed in Claim Case No.2785/2018, whereby challenging the quantum of compensation.

Initially, the claim was filed by the mother and father of the deceased, however,
during pendency of the claim petition father died on 28.2.2022.
Hence, his name was deleted.
2. The facts relevant for the purpose of the present case are that on 29.4.2018 at around 12.30 in the afternoon deceased Arun @ Rahul alongwith his friend Manish was going by motorcycle.

When he reached near Deendayal Garden, Bhanwarkuwa, respondent No.1 came riding motorcycle No.MP-09-QM-9077 in rash and negligent manner, dashed into the motorcycle of deceased,
because of which Arun fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was rushed to Medi Square Hospital, where he died NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35632 2 MA-2088-2022 during treatment.
2.1 The claim petition was filed by the claimants as mentioned above under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation.

The claims Tribunal after recording evidence concluded that it was the mistake on the part of the insured vehicle, which caused accident resulting into death of deceased and a total compensation of Rs.9,80,000/- was awarded to the appellants.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claims Tribunal while quantifying compensation has deducted 50% from the income of deceased Arun considering the fact that he was a bachelor.

Apart from this, the Tribunal also discarded the income as claimed by the appellant based on Income-tax returns on the ground that apart from singular Income-tax return for one year there was no material to establish the source of income of the deceased and not even document regarding establishment of shop were present.

As such, his income was considered on notional basis Smt. Saraswatinbai vs Arvind on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105253008/
1 at Rs.6,000/- per month treating him an unskilled Labour.
Learned counsel submits that in the Income-tax return for the A.Y.2017-2018 (F.Y. 2016-2017) Ex.P/16 the source of income of deceased has been mentioned as income from cyber cafe.
Thus, the return itself disclosed that the deceased was earning from running cyber cafe.
He also points out that there was bank statement before the Tribunal, which would show that the deceased was earning from running his business of cyber cafe.
He further submits that no addition has been made by the Tribunal under the head of future prospects, although deceased was 24 years of age at the time of his accident.
He further submits that meager NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35632 3 MA-2088-2022 amount has been awarded in other heads.

He further points out that there was no occasion to doubt the Income-tax returns, which were placed on record before the Tribunal as subsequently the acknowledgment of the same was brought on record by way of filing application under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC.
He, thus prays for upward revision of compensation.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company while opposing the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant, submits that a bare perusal of Income-tax return for the year 2016-2017 would show that NIL tax was paid by the deceased.
He submits that the same appears to be an effort to build capital and not a clinching proof to show the source of income of the deceased.

He submits that claim of the appellant that deceased was running cyber cafe was asserted, however,
not a single document was filed before the Tribunal like necessary permission for the same,
registration number, educational qualification of the deceased, nothing has been placed on record to show that the deceased was capable for running such kind of business.
The bank statement, which were filed before the Tribunal would show that he was not earning such amount from the said shop.
He, thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.

6. The singular bone of contention of the present case is that the Income-tax return for the year 2017-2018 Ex.P/16 has not been taken into account by the Tribunal rather it has incorrectly been discarded in para 20 by submitting that based on singular Income-tax return it would not be proper to assess the income according to the same.

This Court, while going through NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35632 4 MA-2088-2022 the record of the claims Tribunal has not found any material whatsoever, which would prima facie demonstrate that the deceased was running cyber cafe, even the bank statement of account of the deceased are not indicative of this fact.
Thus, in the considered view of this Court interference with respect to the conclusion drawn by the claims Tribunal regarding claim based on Income-tax return is not warranted.
However, considering the fact that the deceased before his death filed Income-tax return and claimed that he was running a business treating him as unskilled Labour does not appear to be correct.
Hence, by treating him as a semi skilled Labour his income is hereby taken at Rs.8,500/- per month in the peculiar facts of the present case.

7. Considering the fact that he was 24 years of age at the time of accident, 40% addition is made in his income in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 .

In view of the above additions and modifications, now the differential amount comes to Rs.3,43,600/-, which shall be paid to the appellant over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing claim petition till its payment.

9. With the aforesaid modification, the present Misc.Appeal stands NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35632 5 MA-2088-2022 disposed off.

10. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that looking to the peculiar facts of the present case that son and husband of the appellant both have died and she remains alone the excess Court fees deposited by her be directed to be refunded.

11. Considering the extraordinary facts of the present case office is directed to verify this fact and refund the excess Court fees to the appellant.
